_meta.purpose: Complete content package for CC to add to the TFA STIX bundle. All objects are CC-ready with full public content, technical descriptions, SAFE IDs, coordinates, lifecycle phases, and extension fields.
_meta.id_range: SAFE-T-0146 through SAFE-T-0165 (parent techniques), plus sub-techniques
_meta.instructions_for_cc: Each object below needs to be converted to a full STIX attack-pattern with all x_safe_* extension fields, x_mitre_* compat fields, kill_chain_phases (all three kill chains), external_references, and object_marking_refs. Use the SAFE STIX template v1.3.0 as the structural reference. Also create mitigates/indicates relationships for any mitigations/indicators that apply.

new_tactics.name: Grooming & Targeted Recruitment
new_tactics.description: Techniques for building exploitative relationships via technology. Covers child grooming, romance fraud initiation, and trafficking recruitment. The perpetrator uses technology to identify, approach, build trust with, desensitise, and ultimately exploit a target.
new_tactics.x_safe_public_intro: These are ways someone might use technology to build a relationship with you (or your child) specifically to exploit, control, or harm you later. It often starts with flattery, attention, and gifts — and gradually crosses boundaries.
new_tactics.x_safe_public_safety: If you or your child is being contacted by someone who seems 'too good to be true' — especially if they're pushing for private communication, asking personal questions quickly, or making you feel obligated — trust that instinct. Contact 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or, for children, Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800).

new_tactics.name: Discovery & Preparation
new_tactics.description: How perpetrators learn, discover, and acquire the tools and techniques for technology-facilitated abuse. The pre-attack phase — understanding where someone learns to install stalkerware, discovers AirTag tracking, or is recruited into scam operations. Prevention-focused tactic for NFPs, law enforcement, and educators.
new_tactics.x_safe_public_name: How People Learn to Do This
new_tactics.x_safe_public_intro: Understanding where and how people learn abusive techniques helps us prevent harm before it starts. These patterns show how surveillance tools are normalised, how controlling behaviours are taught, and where intervention is most effective.
new_tactics.x_safe_public_safety: If you recognise these patterns in someone you know — or in yourself — support is available. Reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Contact 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732).

new_techniques.name: Online Target Identification
new_techniques.description: Using social media, dating platforms, forums, or gaming platforms to identify and select potential victims based on vulnerability indicators such as loneliness, recent breakup, financial difficulty, age, or naivety. The perpetrator scouts for targets before making contact, often reviewing profiles, post history, and public information to assess susceptibility.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone may be watching your online activity to target you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Before making contact, some people carefully study social media profiles, dating app activity, or online posts to find someone they think they can manipulate. They look for signs of loneliness, recent heartbreak, financial stress, or trusting nature.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: A stranger seems to know a lot about you from the start
x_safe_public_notices.detail: They reference things from your profile, posts, or comments in a way that feels like they've done research.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Someone contacts you right after you've posted about something difficult
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Predators and scammers monitor for vulnerability signals like breakup posts, grief, or financial stress.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The approach feels perfectly tailored to you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: They share your exact interests, values, or experiences — it feels like destiny but may be calculated.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Review what's public on your profiles
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Check what strangers can see on your social media, dating profiles, and forum accounts. Consider limiting what's visible.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Be cautious with new contacts who seem to know you well
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If someone you've just met seems unusually attuned to your situation, that may be strategic rather than genuine connection.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to your children about online stranger contact
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Help young people understand that adults who contact them online may have studied their profiles first.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Frame this as awareness, not fear — the goal is informed caution.

sub_techniques.name: Dating Platform Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Using dating apps (Tinder, Bumble, Hinge, Grindr) to identify targets, often filtering for vulnerability signals in profiles such as recently single status, mentions of loneliness, or indicators of financial situation.
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Someone uses dating apps to find people they can exploit — looking for signs of vulnerability in profiles and conversations.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They move very fast emotionally
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Intense declarations of feelings within days. This pace is designed to overwhelm your judgement.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They want to move off the dating app quickly
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Pushing to WhatsApp, Telegram, or phone calls before you're comfortable removes the platform's safety features.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Keep conversations on the platform initially
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Dating apps have reporting and blocking features. Moving to private messaging removes those protections.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Do a reverse image search on their photos
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Scammers often use stolen photos. A reverse image search can reveal if the photos belong to someone else.

sub_techniques.name: Gaming Platform Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Identifying targets (often minors) via gaming platforms (Roblox, Minecraft, Fortnite, Discord) based on age indicators, activity patterns, in-game behaviour, and willingness to engage in chat. Groomers look for children who seem isolated, eager for attention, or responsive to gifts.
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Adults use gaming platforms to find children they can build relationships with. They look for kids who seem lonely, who respond to attention, or who accept in-game gifts.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: An older player is giving your child lots of attention
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Buying them in-game items, always wanting to play together, asking personal questions.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child has a new 'best friend' online they won't talk about
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Secrecy about online friendships is a warning sign, especially with age gaps.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child is receiving gifts (game currency, items, subscriptions)
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Gift-giving creates obligation and is a classic grooming technique.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Know what games your child plays and who they play with
x_safe_public_actions.detail: You don't need to monitor every message, but understanding who they interact with regularly matters.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Frame this as interest in their world, not surveillance.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Set up parental controls on gaming platforms
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Most platforms have settings to limit who can contact your child or send friend requests.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report to ACCCE if you're concerned about an adult contacting your child
x_safe_public_actions.detail: The Australian Centre to Counter Child Exploitation: accce.gov.au/report

sub_techniques.name: Social Media Target Selection
sub_techniques.description: Identifying targets via Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, Facebook based on public posts, follower counts, content themes, geographic indicators, or visible vulnerability. Both child and adult targeting occurs through social media.
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Someone studies your social media activity to decide whether and how to approach you. Public posts, check-ins, relationship status, and even the tone of your captions can be used to assess vulnerability.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: A stranger follows you and immediately starts engaging with all your content
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Liking old posts, commenting on everything, sharing your stories — creating a sense of connection quickly.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They seem to share all your interests and values
x_safe_public_notices.detail: This mirroring is a common manipulation technique — they've read your profile and are reflecting it back.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Set your accounts to private
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Limit who can see your posts, stories, and personal information.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Be cautious about what you share publicly
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Location check-ins, relationship updates, and emotional posts can all be used to assess your vulnerability.

new_techniques.name: Trust Building & Love Bombing
new_techniques.description: Overwhelming the target with attention, affection, compliments, gifts, or constant communication to create emotional dependency and false intimacy. In romance fraud, this is the 'fattening' phase. In child grooming, this is the befriending stage. The perpetrator mirrors the target's interests, validates their feelings, and positions themselves as uniquely understanding and trustworthy.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is overwhelming you with attention and affection
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They message constantly, shower you with compliments, say you're 'the only one who understands them,' and make you feel like the centre of their world. This intensity feels amazing — but healthy relationships don't start at full speed.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The relationship is moving incredibly fast
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Declarations of love within days or weeks. Talking about a future together before you've really gotten to know each other.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They're available all the time
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Instant responses to every message, always wanting to talk, checking in constantly. It feels attentive but it's creating dependency.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They mirror everything about you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: They love the same music, share the same values, have the same dreams. It feels like soulmates but may be calculated reflection.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They share 'deep secrets' to create false intimacy
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Telling you vulnerable things about themselves early on to encourage you to do the same. This creates a sense of mutual trust that hasn't been earned.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: You feel guilty when you're not available to them
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If you don't respond quickly or need space, they make you feel like you've hurt them. This is the obligation forming.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Slow down
x_safe_public_actions.detail: A genuine connection will still be there next week, next month. If someone can't handle you taking things at a comfortable pace, that tells you something.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Maintain your other relationships
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If you're spending less time with friends and family because of this new person, notice that shift.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Ask yourself: would I accept this pace from anyone else?
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Remove the feelings for a moment and look at the behaviour pattern. Is this how healthy relationships normally start?

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to someone you trust about the relationship
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Describe what's happening to a friend, family member, or counsellor. Outside perspective can see patterns you're too close to notice.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Use a safe device if you think your communications might be monitored.

sub_techniques.name: Gift & Financial Grooming
sub_techniques.description: Sending gifts, game currency, gift cards, small amounts of money, or paying for things to build obligation and emotional debt. In gaming contexts, buying in-game items for minors. In romance fraud, sending flowers or small transfers. Creates reciprocity pressure — the target feels they 'owe' something in return.
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is giving you gifts to create obligation
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They buy you things, send money, pay for meals, or give your child in-game items. This feels generous but it creates a feeling of owing them — which they will eventually use.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The gifts come before you've established a real relationship
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Generosity from someone you barely know is a warning sign, not a green flag.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: You feel uncomfortable saying no to their requests because of what they've given you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: This is the obligation working exactly as intended.

x_safe_public_actions.action: You don't owe anyone anything because they gave you something
x_safe_public_actions.detail: A genuine gift has no strings attached. If you feel pressure to reciprocate, that's a signal.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Tell your children: adults shouldn't be buying them things online
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Especially from people they don't know in person.

new_techniques.name: Boundary Testing & Desensitisation
new_techniques.description: Making incrementally escalating requests to test compliance and normalise boundary violations. Starts small (share your location, send a photo, stay up late talking) and escalates (send intimate content, meet in person, transfer money, cut off contact with friends). The request-demand-threaten-force escalation sequence. Each compliance makes the next request harder to refuse.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is pushing your boundaries and it keeps getting worse
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: It started with small requests — share your location, let me see your phone, send a photo. Over time the requests got bigger, more personal, more uncomfortable. When you say no, they react badly. This pattern of testing what they can get you to do is not normal relationship behaviour.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Requests start small and gradually get bigger
x_safe_public_notices.detail: They might start by asking you to share your location 'so they know you're safe,' then escalate to wanting access to your messages, then your passwords.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They guilt-trip you when you say no
x_safe_public_notices.detail: 'If you loved me you would...' or 'I thought you trusted me.' Making you feel bad for having boundaries.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They frame boundary violations as proof of love
x_safe_public_notices.detail: 'I only check your phone because I care.' Normal relationships don't require giving up your privacy.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: You feel like you 'owe' them something
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Especially after they've given you gifts, attention, or support — this creates a sense of obligation that they exploit.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Things that felt uncomfortable now feel normal
x_safe_public_notices.detail: You've gradually adjusted to behaviour that would have alarmed you at the start. This is desensitisation — and it's deliberate.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Trust your discomfort
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If something feels wrong, it probably is. You don't need to justify saying no.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to someone you trust
x_safe_public_actions.detail: A friend, family member, counsellor, or helpline. Describe the pattern, not just individual incidents.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Use a safe device if you think your communications are monitored.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Know that this is a pattern, not a one-off
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If requests keep escalating and 'no' is never accepted, this is a control pattern. It's not about this one request — it's about establishing that your boundaries don't matter.

new_techniques.name: Isolation from Protective Networks
new_techniques.description: Encouraging or engineering the target's separation from friends, family, or online communities who might recognise the grooming pattern. 'They don't understand us.' 'Your parents wouldn't get it.' 'Your friends are jealous.' Undermines existing relationships to increase dependency on the perpetrator.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is trying to separate you from the people who care about you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They suggest your friends don't really understand you, your family is too controlling, or that other people are jealous of your relationship. Gradually, they become the only person you feel you can talk to. This isn't love — it's isolation.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They criticise your friends and family
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Subtle at first — 'I just think they don't appreciate you' — then more directly undermining your relationships.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They want to be your only source of support
x_safe_public_notices.detail: 'You don't need them, you have me.' Creating a world where they're the centre.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: You're spending less time with people who matter to you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If your social world has shrunk since this relationship started, notice that.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They react badly when you make plans without them
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Guilt, anger, sulking, or accusations when you spend time with others.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Maintain your existing relationships
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Keep seeing friends and family, even if the other person doesn't like it. The people who were there before this relationship are your safety net.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Notice if your world is getting smaller
x_safe_public_actions.detail: A healthy relationship adds to your life — it doesn't replace everything else in it.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Tell someone what's happening
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If you feel like you can't talk to anyone about this relationship, that itself is a warning sign.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Use a safe device to reach out if needed.

evidence_types: Social network analysis showing relationship reduction
Message content showing undermining of other relationships

new_techniques.name: Migration to Private/Encrypted Platforms
new_techniques.description: Moving communication from public or monitored platforms to private, encrypted, or ephemeral channels (Telegram, Signal, Snapchat, WhatsApp) to avoid detection by parents, platform moderation, or law enforcement. Framed as 'more personal' or 'more private' but the purpose is removing safety infrastructure.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: They want to move your conversations somewhere more 'private'
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They suggest moving from a dating app, gaming platform, or social media to a private messaging app — 'so we can talk properly.' This removes the safety features of the original platform and makes the conversation harder for anyone else to see.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They push to move off the original platform early
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Before you've really gotten to know them, they want to switch to WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, or phone calls.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They specifically want ephemeral messaging
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Snapchat (messages disappear), Telegram (secret chats), Signal (disappearing messages) — they want conversations that don't leave a trail.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They frame it as romantic or special
x_safe_public_notices.detail: 'I want to talk to you properly, not on here.' It sounds sweet but it removes your safety net.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Keep conversations on the original platform until you're comfortable
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Dating apps, gaming platforms, and social media have reporting and blocking features. Private messaging doesn't.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Ask yourself why they need to move platforms
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If someone is genuine, they'll be happy to keep talking wherever you're comfortable.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Tell your children: if an online friend wants to move to a different app, tell an adult
x_safe_public_actions.detail: This is one of the clearest warning signs in child grooming.

sub_techniques.name: Snapchat Exploitation
sub_techniques.description: Using Snapchat's disappearing messages and Snap Map features specifically because content auto-deletes, reducing evidence. Quick Add and Snap Map enable contact with minors based on location proximity. The ephemeral nature of Snapchat makes it the platform of choice for grooming conversations that the perpetrator doesn't want recorded.
sub_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Snapchat messages disappear after viewing, which means there's less evidence. Someone may specifically choose Snapchat for conversations they don't want anyone else to see.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They only want to talk on Snapchat, not other platforms
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If someone insists on Snapchat specifically, consider why they want disappearing messages.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child has Snapstreaks with people they don't know in person
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Maintaining daily Snap streaks creates a sense of obligation and routine contact.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Disable Snap Map or set to Ghost Mode
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Snap Map shows your real-time location to friends. Ghost Mode hides your location from everyone.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Parents: review your child's Snapchat friend list
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Look for contacts they don't know in person, especially adults.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Have the conversation about why, not just what you're checking.

new_techniques.name: Age/Identity Deception
new_techniques.description: Misrepresenting age, identity, appearance, occupation, or circumstances to build trust. Includes catfishing, using stolen photos, creating false personas, and age misrepresentation by adults targeting minors or by scammers targeting adults. The deception is the foundation on which the exploitative relationship is built.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: The person you're talking to may not be who they say they are
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They might be using someone else's photos, lying about their age, inventing a life story, or pretending to be someone they're not. Online, identity is easy to fake — and some people build entire false personas to exploit others.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They won't video call or always have an excuse
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If someone avoids showing their face live, they may not look like their photos.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Their story has inconsistencies
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Details about their life, job, location, or past don't add up or change over time.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: A reverse image search shows their photos belong to someone else
x_safe_public_notices.detail: This is a strong indicator of catfishing or scam activity.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They claim to be younger/older than they appear
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Especially concerning when an adult claims to be a teenager to contact minors.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Do a reverse image search
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Right-click their profile photo and search Google Images, or use TinEye. If the photo appears elsewhere with a different name, it's likely stolen.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Video call before meeting in person
x_safe_public_actions.detail: A genuine person will be happy to video call. Persistent refusal is a red flag.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to children about online identity deception
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Help young people understand that the person they're talking to online may not be who they claim.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Frame this as 'people online can pretend to be anyone' rather than creating fear.

new_techniques.name: Livestream Exploitation
new_techniques.description: Using livestreaming platforms (Twitch, YouTube Live, TikTok Live, Instagram Live) to make initial contact with minors, build relationships through donations/gifts, engage in chat, and move to private communication. Livestreaming provides a parasocial dynamic where the viewer feels a personal connection to the streamer, which groomers exploit.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Adults watch children's livestreams and use the chat, donations, or direct messages to build a relationship. The attention and gifts feel exciting — but an adult consistently engaging with a child's livestream is a warning sign.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child is receiving donations or gifts from adult viewers
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Money or virtual gifts from strangers during livestreams create obligation.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: An adult viewer is consistently present and commenting
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Regular engagement from an adult in a child's chat is concerning.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The viewer moves to direct messaging
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Moving from public chat to private DMs is a key escalation step.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child is livestreaming to strangers
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Children may not understand that livestreaming is broadcasting to an unknown audience.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to your child about who watches their streams
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Help them understand that their audience includes strangers, and that adult attention isn't always positive.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Set livestreaming accounts to friends-only or disable
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Most platforms allow restricting who can view streams and comment.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report concerning adults to the platform and ACCCE
x_safe_public_actions.detail: accce.gov.au/report for child exploitation concerns.

new_techniques.name: AI-Assisted Grooming
new_techniques.description: Using AI chatbots, LLMs, or automated messaging to maintain multiple grooming relationships simultaneously at scale. AI enables personalised, varied manipulation conversations that adapt to each target's responses. The 'pig butchering' industrial model uses AI to manage hundreds of simultaneous relationships, with human operators stepping in for high-value interactions.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: The person you're talking to might be a chatbot — or managed by AI
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Scam operations now use AI to have convincing conversations with many people at once. The messages feel personal and genuine, but they're generated by software designed to build trust and extract money or compliance.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Responses come at unusual hours with no delay
x_safe_public_notices.detail: AI doesn't sleep. If someone always responds instantly, regardless of time zone, that's worth noticing.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Their writing style is very consistent and polished
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Real humans have typos, moods, and variations. AI-generated messages can be unnaturally consistent.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They never make mistakes or reference real-world spontaneous events
x_safe_public_notices.detail: AI conversations can feel perfect but lack the messiness of real life.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They deflect or change subject when you ask specific questions
x_safe_public_notices.detail: AI-managed conversations struggle with unexpected, specific, or off-script questions.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Ask unexpected, specific questions
x_safe_public_actions.detail: What's the weather like where you are right now? What did you have for breakfast? Real people answer easily. AI-managed conversations stumble.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Insist on a live video call
x_safe_public_actions.detail: This is the single most effective way to verify you're talking to a real person. If they won't or can't, be very cautious.

x_safe_public_actions.action: If they ask for money, it's almost certainly a scam
x_safe_public_actions.detail: No matter how real the relationship feels, if money is requested — it's the extraction phase.

new_techniques.name: Sextortion-as-Grooming
new_techniques.description: The pattern where initial sextortion of a minor transitions into ongoing control and exploitation. The first coerced image becomes permanent leverage for escalating demands — more images, sexual acts, money, or compliance. The perpetrator uses shame and fear of parental discovery as ongoing leverage. This is the intersection of grooming and sextortion responsible for a significant number of teen male suicides.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is using intimate images to control you or your child
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They convinced you (or your child) to share an intimate image, and now they're using it as leverage — demanding more images, money, or compliance. The threat of exposure feels overwhelming, but compliance almost always leads to escalation, not safety.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_safety_warning: If you or your child is experiencing this: do not comply with further demands. Compliance almost never stops the demands — it escalates them. This is not your fault, regardless of what was shared. Help is available and this can be stopped.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Demands escalate after the first image is shared
x_safe_public_notices.detail: What started as one image becomes demands for more, for video, for money, for meeting in person.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Threats to send images to friends, family, or school
x_safe_public_notices.detail: The perpetrator uses the victim's social network as leverage — 'I'll send this to everyone you know.'

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your child suddenly becomes withdrawn, anxious, or changes device behaviour
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Secrecy about their phone, staying up late, emotional distress — these can indicate sextortion.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Unexplained money transfers from your child's accounts
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Some sextortion demands are financial — the child may be sending money to make it stop.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Stop all communication with the person making demands
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Block them on every platform. Do not respond to threats. They are counting on your fear.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: If you're concerned about immediate safety, contact police.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Do not pay or send more content
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Paying or complying does not make it stop. It proves the leverage works and demands will escalate.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report to the eSafety Commissioner
x_safe_public_actions.detail: The eSafety Commissioner can issue takedown notices to platforms and help with image removal. esafety.gov.au

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to your child with compassion, not anger
x_safe_public_actions.detail: They are the victim. Their biggest fear is your reaction. Respond with support and they'll let you help.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: What they need to hear: 'This is not your fault. I'm not angry. We will sort this out together.'

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report to police and ACCCE for child victims
x_safe_public_actions.detail: This is a crime. accce.gov.au/report for child exploitation. Police for all victims.

evidence_types: Message logs showing demands and threats

new_techniques.name: Stalkerware Marketing Discovery
new_techniques.description: Encountering commercial stalkerware products through advertising, search results, or app store listings. Products marketed as 'parental monitoring' or 'employee tracking' normalise surveillance and provide accessible tools for intimate partner abuse. The marketing language ('keep your family safe,' 'know where your kids are') frames surveillance as care.

new_techniques.name: Manosphere & Misogynist Content Exposure
new_techniques.description: Exposure to online content promoting control, surveillance, and abuse of partners as normal or desirable. Includes 'red pill' communities, incel forums, Andrew Tate ecosystem, pickup artist material, and 'alpha male' content. These communities normalise coercive control, frame surveillance as rational, and teach manipulation techniques as 'relationship skills.'
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Online content that teaches controlling behaviour as 'normal'
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Some online communities and influencers teach that monitoring your partner, controlling their behaviour, and using manipulation are normal parts of relationships. This content radicalises people — often young men — into believing abuse is acceptable.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Someone in your life starts using language about 'high value' people or 'alpha' behaviour
x_safe_public_notices.detail: This language often comes from communities that normalise control and dehumanise partners.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They talk about relationships in transactional terms
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Viewing relationships as exchanges of value rather than partnerships of equals is a red flag.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They justify monitoring or controlling behaviour as 'protecting' the relationship
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Framing surveillance as care is a learned pattern from these communities.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Recognise the pattern
x_safe_public_actions.detail: If someone's attitude toward relationships has changed after consuming specific online content, the content may be the problem.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Talk to young people about what they're watching
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Many teenagers encounter this content through algorithm recommendations on YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: Approach with curiosity, not judgement — 'what are you watching?' not 'that's terrible.'

new_techniques.name: Forum & Community Technique Sharing
new_techniques.description: Learning specific abuse techniques from online forums, Reddit communities, Facebook groups, or messaging channels where perpetrators share methods. Includes 'how to catch a cheating partner' communities that teach surveillance, tracking forums, and groups sharing stalkerware recommendations.

sub_techniques.name: Domestic Surveillance Forum Pipeline
sub_techniques.description: Specific subreddits, Facebook groups, and forums framed as 'catching a cheating partner' that teach surveillance and control techniques. The framing as 'justified' surveillance normalises the behaviour. Users don't self-identify as perpetrators — they see themselves as victims of infidelity exercising reasonable vigilance.

new_techniques.name: Peer-to-Peer Technique Transfer
new_techniques.description: Learning surveillance or control techniques from friends, family members, colleagues, or social contacts who share what 'worked' for them. Informal knowledge transfer in social settings. 'My mate told me about this app that tracks your partner's location.' The technique is normalised because it comes from a trusted source.
evidence_types: App installation timelines correlating with social contact

new_techniques.name: AI-Assisted Targeting Discovery
new_techniques.description: Using AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, search engines, coding assistants) to research surveillance methods, learn how to track someone, or develop manipulation strategies. AI lowers the skill barrier — someone who couldn't write code can now generate a keylogger. AI platforms actively try to prevent this but it remains a cat-and-mouse game.

new_techniques.name: Scam Compound Recruitment & Training
new_techniques.description: Being recruited into organised fraud/scam operations (often through false job advertisements) and trained in romance fraud, sextortion, and social engineering techniques at scale. Recruited individuals are often themselves trafficked and exploited. The 'Nigerian Prince' industrial pipeline — from recruitment to training to operation. Some operators are coerced, others are willing participants.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Organised scam operations train people to exploit you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: The romance scam or sextortion you're experiencing may be run by an organised operation that recruits, trains, and manages dozens of scammers. The person messaging you may themselves be a victim of trafficking, following a script provided by criminal operators.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The scam feels professional and well-rehearsed
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Multiple stages, consistent messaging, coordinated pressure — this is an operation, not one person.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They shift from emotional to financial requests in a predictable pattern
x_safe_public_notices.detail: The 'pig butchering' model follows a documented sequence: build trust → introduce investment opportunity → extract funds.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report to ReportCyber (cyber.gov.au)
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Australian Cyber Security Centre's reporting mechanism for cybercrime.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Report to your bank immediately if money has been sent
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Some transactions can be reversed if reported quickly.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Don't blame yourself
x_safe_public_actions.detail: These operations are designed by professionals specifically to exploit human trust. Being targeted is not a reflection of your intelligence.

new_techniques.name: Child Device Monitoring Abuse
new_techniques.description: Using parental monitoring on children's devices to surveil an ex-partner's activities, location, and communications through the child. The child's device becomes a surveillance tool against the other parent. Distinct from Child Custody Tech Abuse (SAFE-T-0145) where the child is the target — here the child is the vector.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone may be using your child's devices to monitor you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Your ex-partner may have installed monitoring software or configured parental controls on your children's devices — not to protect the children, but to track your location, read your messages through the child, or monitor what happens in your home.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_safety_warning: Be careful about discussing sensitive matters near your children's devices if you suspect monitoring. Consider whether devices given to children by the other parent may have monitoring enabled.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your ex seems to know details about your home life they shouldn't know
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Conversations, visitors, your schedule — information that could only come from inside your home.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The children's devices have parental monitoring you didn't set up
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Check for apps like Life360, Find My, or other tracking/monitoring apps on devices provided by the other parent.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Your ex references your location when the children are with you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If they know where you went while the children had their devices, the devices may be tracking.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Check children's devices for monitoring apps
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Look for parental control apps, location sharing, and device administrator settings you didn't configure.
x_safe_public_actions.safety_note: If you find monitoring, get advice before removing it — the other parent may be alerted.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Consider a separate device for sensitive communication
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Keep important calls and messages off any device the children carry between homes.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Document and seek legal advice
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Using children's devices for surveillance may violate family court orders and surveillance legislation.

new_techniques.name: AI-Generated Evidence Fabrication
new_techniques.description: Using AI to create fake text message screenshots, fabricated legal documents, forged emails, synthetic audio recordings, or manipulated metadata for use in legal proceedings, custody disputes, or reputation attacks. Distinct from Deepfake Creation (visual media) — this is documentary evidence fabrication. AI lowers the skill barrier for creating convincing fakes that can fool courts, employers, and support services.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone may be using AI to create fake evidence against you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: AI can now generate convincing fake text message screenshots, emails, documents, and even audio recordings. Someone may use these fakes in court, with your employer, with child protection, or to damage your reputation.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Evidence is presented that shows conversations you never had
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Screenshots of messages you didn't send, emails you didn't write, documents you didn't create.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The evidence seems too perfect
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Real conversations are messy. Fabricated ones can be unnaturally clean, perfectly supporting the other person's narrative.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Metadata doesn't match
x_safe_public_notices.detail: A forensic examiner can check whether screenshots, documents, or recordings have been generated or manipulated.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Preserve your own records
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Keep your actual message history, emails, and documents. Your real records are the best defence against fabricated ones.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Request forensic analysis of suspicious evidence
x_safe_public_actions.detail: AI-generated content often has detectable artefacts. A digital forensic expert can identify fabrication.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Alert your lawyer to the possibility of AI fabrication
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Courts are increasingly aware of this issue but your legal team needs to know to challenge suspect evidence.

new_techniques.name: Weaponised Welfare Checks
new_techniques.description: Repeatedly calling police or child protection services to conduct welfare checks on the victim, using state agencies as a harassment tool. Reports are technically 'concerned' but the pattern is punitive — using volume and frequency to exhaust, intimidate, and signal that the perpetrator can deploy the state against the victim at any time. Distinct from Swatting (immediate physical danger) and Emergency Service Manipulation (false reports for legal advantage).
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is sending police or child protection to your door repeatedly
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: Your ex-partner or someone else is making repeated reports to police, child protection, or other agencies to trigger welfare checks at your home. Each individual report may seem 'concerned,' but the pattern is harassment — designed to exhaust you, intimidate you, and signal that they can bring the state to your door whenever they want.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Police or child protection visit you repeatedly based on reports from the same person
x_safe_public_notices.detail: A pattern of unsubstantiated reports from one source is harassment, not genuine concern.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: The reports coincide with custody disputes or conflict
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Reports that arrive right before court dates or during disagreements are tactical, not protective.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Each report is unfounded but they keep coming
x_safe_public_notices.detail: The perpetrator knows the reports won't lead to action — the check itself is the weapon.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Document every welfare check
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Record dates, times, what was reported, by whom, and the outcome. This pattern is your evidence.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Ask responding officers to note the pattern in their records
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Police can flag repeated unsubstantiated reports from the same complainant.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Seek legal advice about vexatious reporting
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Repeatedly making false or malicious reports may itself be an offence and can be raised in family court.

new_techniques.name: Legal System Abuse / Litigation Abuse
new_techniques.description: Using repeated court applications, vexatious claims, subpoenas, discovery requests, or procedural motions as financial and psychological weapons. Filing and withdrawing AVOs, repeated custody variations, dragging out property settlements, issuing subpoenas to employers or therapists. Each action costs the victim money and emotional energy. The legal system itself becomes the abuse tool. Sometimes called 'systems abuse' or 'paper abuse.'
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: Someone is using the legal system as a weapon against you
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: They keep filing court applications, making legal threats, demanding documents, and dragging out proceedings. Each one costs you money, time, and emotional energy — and they know it. The legal process itself has become the abuse.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Court applications that seem designed to cause you stress rather than achieve an outcome
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Applications that are withdrawn before hearing, filed right before holidays, or repeat issues already resolved.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Legal costs are escalating beyond what the issues warrant
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Spending $50,000 fighting over $5,000 of property isn't about the property.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Every attempt at resolution is met with new demands or applications
x_safe_public_notices.detail: The goal isn't resolution — it's continuation. The process is the punishment.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Subpoenas or discovery requests targeting your support network
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Subpoenaing your therapist's notes, your employer's records, or your friends' messages — using legal process to invade your life.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Document the pattern, not just individual applications
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Courts respond to patterns. A timeline of 15 applications in 12 months tells a story that individual responses don't.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Ask your lawyer about vexatious litigant provisions
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Australian courts can declare someone a vexatious litigant, requiring leave before filing further applications.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Seek a family violence-informed lawyer
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Not all family lawyers understand systems abuse. Find one who recognises litigation as a form of control.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Access legal aid or pro bono services if costs are unsustainable
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Financial exhaustion is part of the strategy. Legal aid, community legal centres, and Women's Legal Services can help.

new_techniques.name: Post-Separation App Weaponisation
new_techniques.description: Exploiting court-mandated communication apps (OurFamilyWizard, AppClose, Talking Parents) for microcontrol, excessive documentation demands, or manipulative communication that technically complies with court orders but is designed to exhaust and control. Weaponising the 'paper trail' feature to create false evidence of the other parent's non-compliance. The apps meant to protect victims become tools of abuse.
new_techniques.x_safe_public_title: The co-parenting app has become another tool of control
new_techniques.x_safe_public_summary: The court-ordered communication app was supposed to make things safer, but they're using it to send dozens of messages a day, demand immediate responses, document everything you do, and create a record that makes you look non-compliant. The app that was meant to protect you has become another weapon.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Dozens of messages a day about trivial matters
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Asking what the children ate for breakfast, requesting photos of homework, demanding updates on every activity — the volume is the weapon.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: Every message is carefully worded to sound reasonable in isolation
x_safe_public_notices.detail: Each individual message looks fine. It's the pattern — the volume, the demands, the tone — that constitutes abuse.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: They screenshot and use your response times against you
x_safe_public_notices.detail: 'She took 4 hours to respond about pickup' — using the app's documentation features to build a false narrative.

x_safe_public_notices.signal: You feel anxious every time you get a notification from the app
x_safe_public_notices.detail: If a communication tool causes dread, it's not functioning as intended.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Set boundaries on response times
x_safe_public_actions.detail: You don't need to respond immediately to every message. Set a reasonable schedule (e.g., checking the app twice daily) and document it.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Keep responses brief and factual
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Don't engage with provocative messages. 'Noted' or 'Confirmed' are complete responses.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Document the pattern for your lawyer
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Screenshot the volume — 47 messages in one day about lunch choices is evidence of harassment, not co-parenting.

x_safe_public_actions.action: Raise it with the court
x_safe_public_actions.detail: Courts are increasingly aware of app weaponisation. The pattern of misuse can be raised and orders can be amended.
